claim: McQueen et al. are an example of mean time to compromise (MTTC) as an attacker-side MTD effectiveness metric (Table 3.1, 'examples from the works surveyed')
quote: In a case study, the model was used to aid in a risk reduction estimate between a baseline Supervisory Control
locator: Abstract, preprint PDF p. 2 (only the preprint and a session md are saved; no published copy)
issue: McQueen is the origin of time-to-compromise, but as a SCADA risk-reduction model, not an MTD evaluation; the caption frames the cells as MTD metrics with examples from works surveyed. It is lineage, not an MTD example.
fix_text: acceptable as the metric's origin; optionally note origin vs MTD use in the 4.5 definition instead

claim: Table 4.5: MTTC is sourced to McQueen et al.
quote: We propose a new model for estimating the time to compromise a system component that is visible to an attacker. The model provides an estimate of the expected value of the time-to-compromise
locator: Abstract, preprint PDF p. 2; body Sec. 3: 'The time-to-compromise ( Tpi) is defined as the time needed for an attacker to gain some level of privilege p on some system component i.' (PDF p. 4)
issue: McQueen is the right origin for time-to-compromise; the operational definition used (mean over successful runs, to the goal) is Zhang's, which the co-cite carries.

claim: MTTC is the mean time from the start of a run to the attacker reaching its goal, over the runs in which it does (cited to McQueen)
quote: The time-to-compromise ( Tpi) is defined as the time needed for an attacker to gain some level of privilege p on some system component i.
locator: Sec. 3, preprint PDF p. 4; 'only uses the expected value of the time-to-compromise', Sec. 3.4, PDF p. 11
issue: McQueen's time-to-compromise is an analytical expected value per component and privilege level, not a mean over simulation runs to a goal, and has no conditioning on runs that succeed. The definition as written is Zhang's; McQueen supports only the concept.
fix_text: '[mcqueen2006, zhang2023]' -> 'after [mcqueen2006], as [zhang2023] defines it' (or cite only zhang2023 on the definition)
